title: Dataframe record
description: A table of data that a pipeline declares in [dataframes]. Other fields the manifest declares for it are carried as they are.

ref.description: The record's address as named fields: the same address as `id`, with nothing to parse.

pipeline.description: The ID of the pipeline that declares the asset.

location.description: Where the dataframe's content is: a file, a table in a source, or a query run in a source.

path.description: As declared in chartbook.toml, relative to the pipeline's root. May be a glob.

resolved_path.description: Absolute path on the machine that built the index. Absent from a published index.

modified_at.description: When the file, or the newest file the glob names, was last written, in UTC. Absent when not built.

identifier.description: The table, as declared: one to three dot-separated parts.

url.description: The source's url as the manifest declares it: the public part, never credentials. A reader opens the engine through chartbook.backends.source_url() from it.

modified_at.description: When the engine's file was last written, in UTC, for a DuckDB file. Absent for an in-memory engine.

sql.description: The query, in the source's dialect, as declared.

url.description: The source's url as the manifest declares it: the public part, never credentials. A reader opens the engine through chartbook.backends.source_url() from it.

modified_at.description: When the engine's file was last written, in UTC, for a DuckDB file. Absent for an in-memory engine.

content_hash.description: Hash of the asset's content. Absent when its file has not been built.

definition_hash.description: For a table or query: a hash of its definition (identifier or SQL) and its described columns. A table cannot be content-hashed cheaply, so content_hash is absent and this says what the dataframe is defined as.

file_count.description: For a dataframe of many parts (a folder or a glob): how many files it is. Absent for one file, a table or a query.

files.description: For a dataframe of many parts: its first 1000 files, sorted by path; `file_count` says how many there are.

path.description: Relative to the folder, or to the glob's fixed prefix, with forward slashes.

row_count.description: Its rows, from a parquet file's footer. Absent for a file that is not parquet.

partitions.description: The keys of the `key=value` folders it is in, and their values, as text.

format.description: The format the dataframe's file is stored in, as the manifest declares it: parquet, CSV or TSV, JSON lines (gzipped or not), or Arrow IPC (Feather). Absent when the manifest leaves it to the path's ending (`.parquet`, `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.csv.gz`, `.jsonl`, `.ndjson`, `.jsonl.gz`, `.arrow`, `.feather`, `.ipc`); a path whose ending names none is parquet.

read_options.description: The options the manifest gives the reader of a CSV or JSON lines file, by polars' names (`separator`, `schema_overrides`, `infer_schema_length`, ...). `data.load()`, `data.sql()`, the page and this record read the file with them.

columns.description: The physical schema, as data.load() returns it.

inputs.description: IDs of the assets this one was made from.

keep.description: The manifest marks this asset `keep = true`: every version of its bytes is kept in the store (`store gc` keeps, for each, the newest snapshot holding it), and `chartbook restore` puts it back on disk. Present only when it does.

docs.description: The write-up: the file it is in, or the text itself when it was written inline.

content_hash.description: The hash of the write-up's text, so a build says which text it showed. Write-ups are not pinned; the commit holds them.

date_range.description: The first and last date in `date_col`, in ISO 8601 (a date, or a datetime): how far the data reaches. A date or datetime column as it is; a text column parsed as dates, what does not parse left out. Absent without a `date_col`, for a column with no date in it, or when the data cannot be read.

snapshots.description: Catalog hub versions, newest first, with presence and consecutive-index changes.

glimpse.description: The first rows as text, as the dataframe's page shows them, read when the index described the file. A version rendered from the store shows this without the data. Anyone who can write to a store can write it: shown as text, never read as markup.

last_dates.description: The least and greatest of each column's last non-null date, as text (`N/A` without a date column; `N/A (large file)` over the size threshold), read when the index described the file. Absent when they could not be read.
